translations.text: He bound him with unbreakable iron chains.
Nor did they merely leave him bound on the earth.
Rather, it is written that he threw him into the burning lake of fire—I mean that he is beneath the abyss and the darkness.
And so that you may understand the truth:
We too, my dear ones, since we have understood how great is the joy of this feast laid out for us today,
let us each adorn ourselves inwardly and outwardly, so that we may go to this great banquet today,
so that we may eat the good things prepared for us by Michael, the great warrior of the King of kings.
But since it is a royal banquet,
we ought to wait until they summon,
first, the dignitaries in the king’s court and his great archangel Michael.
Afterward, let us follow them too. Welcome, my dear ones! For whoever humbles himself is exalted
and stands upright. But come, follow me, for look, the great ones
have already gone to Michael’s banquet.
They have been invited. Who are the great ones who were invited first?
Listen attentively.
Adam, Abel, and Seth his son;
Moses, Aaron, Joshua son of Nun, Gideon, Barak, Samson, and the kings David, Solomon, and Hezekiah;
Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, the three holy ones, Elijah, and Elisha—
these great prophets—and Zechariah and his son John, and the twelve apostles,
and Stephen the archdeacon, and the holy elder and priest, Apa Simeon, and the martyrs and all the righteous.
Why am I speaking only of those on earth?
The Lord of glory is there, along with all the heavenly ranks: the angels and archangels, the principalities and authorities,
the cherubim and seraphim,
the thrones, dominions, and powers. They are there,
all of them, glorifying God and his great holy archangel Michael.
But I want to return once more to the court of the archangel Michael,
to these great men of the earth, so that I may question them.
Because of this great feast spread out today,
so that I too may rejoice with those who rejoice, according to the words of the teacher, Paul the apostle.
But I will begin first
with the father of all humanity,
whom God formed according to his likeness and his image. For he is the one I see in the first place
at his reclining place at today's feast, and I will ask him.
Will I dare to speak to him? For I am afraid
and I tremble.
Look, now again I see everyone at today's banquet giving him glory
and honoring him. I too will count myself as one of them,
even though I am a sinner.
I will offer him the joy of my tongue in this way: “Hail, my holy father!
Lord, hail, father of all my ancestors and of all humanity yet to come!”
When I offer him these three expressions of joy, fitting for his glory,
he will certainly cry out in turn, like a father to his son: “Come, you too, and rejoice with us at the great feast spread out for us today.” Having gained the confidence to speak freely before him,
I will ask him, “My lord and father, are you not the one whom God formed with his own hands?
He filled you with the glory of his likeness and his image.
Are you not the one about whom God commanded all the heavenly ranks, ‘Come and bow down before the work of my hands, my likeness and my image’?”
Adam answered, “Yes, my son, I am
the one to whom all these things happened.” We will answer him again, “My lord and father, did not all these things happen, and did not all the angels bow down before you, except
for one alone and his rank?”
He answered, “Yes, my Lord made everything submit to me before I was placed in paradise.”
I will dare to say
to him, “What is your connection with today's feast, since no angel is higher than you? You are the likeness and the image of God.”
But Adam said, “Listen to me, my son,
I am the one who will tell you about the honor of this feast today, because I understand more than you do.
and pay attention. All these things were going to happen at the time when my Lord—
And my God,
and my creator made me according to his likeness and his image.
He adorned me beautifully.
He breathed into me a breath of life.
He seated me on a throne of glory before him.
He commanded all the orders of heaven with his true authority, saying, “Come and worship the work of my hands, my likeness and my image.” Mastema was also there, being the first-created being.
He is the one now called the devil, and he too was an archangel.
Now, when the command came from the Father's mouth,
Michael came, one of the seven angels,
with his entire order, and they worshiped God, our king.
Afterward they worshiped me too, saying, “We worship you, God the creator,
and we worship the one you made according to your likeness and your image.”
Afterward Gabriel came with his entire order, and they worshiped me too, just as Michael had.
Likewise, all the hosts of heaven, according to their order and their ranks.
After all these, the master of Mastema, which means hatred, said:
“You too, come and worship the work of my hands, my likeness and my image, like all your companions.
Satanael answered angrily and said to the Lord, “If there is no rank under you higher than me, except me alone,
and I am next after you in glory, because I am a first-created being, am I now to come and worship dust?
May it never happen that I worship this one! Rather, he is the one who will worship me, because I came before him.”
The Merciful One said, “Satanael, listen to me. I am your God. I am your creator. Come now and worship the work of my hands.”
Mastema said, “May it never happen to me,
neither to me
nor to my entire legion, that we should worship one who is inferior to us.
For we are spirits, but this one is dust. I will not worship him.”
He spoke to him again, a second and a third time: “My first-created being, was it not I who appointed you commander-in-chief under me? I made my angels submit to you.
So now, will you rebel against my kingdom?”
Now will you display disobedience so that it remains forever?
Now will you teach slaves to rise up against their masters?
Now will you show disobedience, Mastema? Are you not my slave? Am I not your Lord?
Do I not have the authority to throw you out of my presence and take my great glory away from you?
This is the glory that no one in my entire kingdom can equal,
except me, my Father, and the Holy Spirit. Obey me and worship the being I have created.
The envious slanderer said before the one to whom everything is subject, “Never shall I worship two lords, neither I nor my entire host.
Indeed, no one in the entire kingdom of heaven is greater than I except you.
And if I wish, I myself, together with my host, will suffice for my entire kingdom on my own.
Never shall I worship someone inferior to me.”
Immediately God, who is free from anger, became angry.
He commanded a great cherub, who struck him and weakened him.
He commanded Michael, who stripped him of his belt and sandal,
along with his staff of light and his sapphire crown.
He took all the glory from him and gave him a garment [?] of darkness, together with all those who were with him. He threw him out of his kingdom.
And Michael did everything that he had been commanded to do.
He seized Satan, stripped him of his power, and threw him out of heaven, together with all those who were with him. He threw him out of his kingdom.
The good God called Michael when he saw his zeal toward the being he had created,
and his fighting on behalf of his Lord.
He said to him in the midst of all his heavenly hosts, “Michael”—which means “power,” while “El” means “God”—“come,” he said, “my holy steward, Michael.
Come, you who fought and won. Come to me, Michael, you who carry out your king’s command.
Look, I have recognized your goodwill toward me and toward all my creation.
I too will direct my goodwill toward you.
Open your mouth, Michael. Receive all my mercies into yourself,
so that you may continue pleading with me at all times on behalf of my likeness and my image.”
I too will forgive them.
For I know that Mastema will fight against my creation, wanting me to cast them away from me, just as I cast him out of my kingdom.
But look, I have appointed you over my creation so that you may save them from his snares.
And you shall plead with me on their behalf.
If they sin, I will forgive them, because I am a merciful God.
Look, Michael, today I appoint you over all the ranks of my kingdom.
And apart from me, my Father, and the Holy Spirit, there is no one greater than you in all the orders of heaven.
O archangel Michael, come and stand at my right hand. Remain close to my throne at all times, commanding all the powers of heaven, who will obey you in everything.
O Michael, you are the one who will teach all the ranks to serve me uprightly. Michael, you are the pride.
And the knowledge of my kingdom.
Lift up your head, which you lowered.
With it you bowed before my creation. I will place upon it this great glory that I took away from the proud one.
Stretch out your hand and take this staff of light for yourself.
Become commander-in-chief in place of the shameful commander-in-chief. O Michael, stretch out your hand, take the staff for yourself, and become commander-in-chief in place of the accuser
of shame. O Michael, stretch out your left hand.
Take this great weapon for yourself and prepare to fight against the enemies of your king.
O Michael, take the sapphire belt for yourself and fasten it around your waist.
So that those who oppose your Lord will see you and quickly be cut down.
Your mouth has been opened, O my minister.
Receive power for yourself.
So that your speech will be like the sound of a crowd speaking.
Come, wear my glory, O Michael.
So that you will teach everyone to give me glory.
Look, I have understood all your goodwill toward my creation.
Come now and serve me throughout the life of my image.
Look at Adam now: you see him there alone, with no one else like him.
But look, I have placed a sign in his side, and it will come into being from him.
Since I have finished saying, O Michael, that it is not good for the man to remain alone,
rather, let us make him a helper suitable for him. O Michael, Adam’s helper, [?] one with him,
from the time when I formed him.
But before bringing her to him, O Michael, if I had created Adam to remain alone—
What need is there for me to plant a paradise, O Michael,
the archangel? This whole world beneath my throne—
I will establish it in the likeness of Adam, which is my image. But now, O Michael,
look, I have appointed you steward over my kingdom, so that you may serve with compassion.
toward the creature I formed.
O Michael, Adam’s descendants will know my name through you.
O Michael, you are the commander-in-chief of the power of heaven. O Michael, ruler
of those in heaven and those on earth, O Michael, you are the sweet fragrance at the time of my holy sacrifice.”
O Michael, you are the one who will present my offering to me on behalf of Adam’s descendants.
Great deeds will be done by Adam’s children. You, O Michael, are the one who will plead for them, so that I may forgive them.
The children of Adam’s line will blaspheme against me because of the one who leads them astray.
But I will forgive them through your pleas, O Michael.
When the Lord had said all these things to Michael,
he stretched out his hand.
He placed the crown on him and made him an archangel.
He placed three seals on him in the form of the Holy Trinity, with the likeness of his image on the seals,
So that the archangel may continually plead with God on behalf of his image. That, then, is why I came to this festival,
which is Michael’s banquet today. I am Adam, your father.
Abel, young and sinless son, I beg you: tell me, you too, about your joy today at Michael’s festival.
“I rejoice,” he said, “because the one whose festival we celebrate today is the one who pleaded with God for my father and my mother until they were forgiven for the transgression they had committed.
And he is the one who took my gifts up to God, until God accepted my sacrifices from me.
He paid no attention to my brother’s offerings, because my brother had not brought them with an upright heart. That is why I rejoice today.”
Seth, I see you rejoicing today at the festival of the holy archangel Michael. “I rejoice,” he said, “because, when Cain killed my brother Abel,
God gave me to my parents as a gift.
And my mother found no milk to nurse me.”
because it had withered from grief for Abel, my brother.
But the archangel Michael is the one who supplies me with my spiritual food from heaven.
That is why I rejoice today.
O righteous Enoch, whom God took away!
Why are you too rejoicing at this feast today? “I rejoice,” he said,
“because I am the one who writes down the sins.
and all the good things of the world in my own hands.
Michael, the holy archangel, is the one who brings them before God, presenting to him the good deeds and the sins too, and pleading with God on their behalf until he has mercy and forgives them.
That is why I rejoice today.”
Methuselah, the righteous old man,
who lived well throughout his days,
“What, then, is your joy today? For I see that you have become cheerful in the midst of this banquet today.”
He said, “Why should I not rejoice? I am the eighth from Adam.
The archangel Michael brought my prayer up to God.
He granted me a long life,
so that my life and my [?] would surpass those of my father Adam: nine hundred and thirty-nine years.
That is why I rejoice today.”
O righteous Noah, are you rejoicing today at the feast of the archangel Michael?
“How could I not rejoice?
For when God became angry and was destroying the world, he put me into an ark with my wife, my children, and all the creatures that move on the earth.
He shut the door of the ark upon us. The floodgates of heaven and earth opened, and they surrounded us.
For forty days and forty nights we did not see the sun,
nor the moon, nor a star.
But Michael, the holy archangel, steered us and the ark.
He kept pleading with God until the water subsided and dry land appeared, so that I and those with me were saved.
That is why I rejoice today.”
Abraham the patriarch, are you too rejoicing today at the feast of the holy archangel Michael? “Yes,” he said, “I rejoice today,
because I am the first person whom Michael visited,
together with my Lord and his other companion, the archangel Gabriel.
And Michael pleaded with God on my behalf, and he gave me Isaac, my son.
And, if indeed I am worthy,
I ate with him beneath the tree of Mamre. That is why I rejoice today.” O righteous
Isaac, the holy promise,
and the holy sacrifice accepted by the living God,
why are you too so splendidly dressed at the feast of the holy archangel Michael? “I am dressed up,” he said, “because I am the only child of my father and mother,
who have no child besides me, nor will they have any after me.
My father bound me by my hands and feet.
He placed me on stones on a deserted mountain.
I saw with my own eyes the knife in my father’s hand, as he was about to slaughter me.
The archangel Michael provided a sheep in my place.
He seized the knife in my father’s hand as he was about to slaughter me.
My sacrifice was completed. That is why I rejoice today.”
The patriarch Jacob, who prevailed with God
and was mighty among men, are you too rejoicing today?
“Yes,” he said, “I rejoice today,
because when my brother Esau pursued me to kill me, I went up to Mesopotamia in Syria, to Laban.
It was Michael who came to me and set apart my wages for me from among the livestock. He blessed me
and my children and my wives. That is why Israel took its name from me.
That is why I rejoice today.”
O Joseph, the righteous and wise man, whom they envied, why are you too rejoicing today?
Joseph said, “Truly, I deserve to rejoice today, because when my brothers envied me, they sold me into a foreign land.
I became poor, miserable, and without anyone, in great distress.
The archangel came to me, rescued me, and made me king.
That is why I rejoice today.
Moses, Aaron, and Joshua son of Nun.
What about you yourselves at this great feast today, the feast of the archangel Michael?
The saints said, “The joy is indeed ours, because Michael is the one who walked with us and his people,
And he cut down our enemies and led the way.
ahead of us into the promised land.
That is indeed why we rejoice today.”
Gideon, I see you too rejoicing today at Michael’s banquet.
“I certainly rejoice,” he said, “because Michael is the one who came to me.
He filled me with his strength, and I went and struck down Midian.
The people were saved. That is why I rejoice today.”
O Manoah, and Anna his wife!
“How great is your joy today?” The judges said, “Truly, we rejoice today, because—”
“We had been childless since our youth; no child had been born to us.
We kept praying and offering sacrifices to God so that we would be remembered. God gave us Samson, the mighty man.
And our other son too rejoices with us today.”
David, the father of Christ according to the flesh,
and the joyful king, I see you today playing your ten-stringed lyre at Michael’s banquet.
David said, “Yes, I rejoice today,
and I dress in finery,
because the verses for all the feasts of the Lord
and of his servants are written on the tablets of my heart.
And the passage that fits this feast today is this: ‘The angel of the Lord surrounds those who fear him,
and rescues them.’ That is why I rejoice today.”
Wise Solomon, are you too rejoicing today? “Yes,” he said, “I rejoice,
because Michael is the one who stood by me from my youth and brought peace throughout my days.”
And he carried my prayer up to God. I built his house; that is why I rejoice today.
Hezekiah, the righteous king, do you not rejoice today at the feast of Michael the archangel?
“Yes,” he said, “I rejoice today,
because when the Assyrians surrounded me and my people, it was Michael the archangel who went and struck them down that night,
185,000 men in all. I too was saved, along with my people. That is why I rejoice today.”
O Isaiah, the great prophet,
what is your joy today, in your turn,
at Michael’s feast? “This is my joy,” he said: “All these torments inflicted on me, and these insults,
by King Manasseh and those with him—
it was Michael the archangel who stood beside me.
He gave me strength until they sawed me in half
with a wooden saw. That is why I rejoice today.”
My holy father Jeremiah,
I see you today with your great lamp of light, rejoicing at the feast of Michael the archangel.
“I rejoice greatly,” he said, “because I spent seventy years in captivity
with my people. The holy archangel Michael
pleaded with the one who lives forever, and he put compassion into the hearts of the Babylonian kings.
They released us, and we returned to Jerusalem.
That is why I rejoice today.”
Ezekiel the prophet, come and tell us why you are leaping for joy today
at the feast of the holy archangel Michael. “I am leaping freely,” he said,
“and rejoicing, because Michael the archangel
brought me a scroll. He gave me a command, and I ate it.
The prophecies were revealed to me.
That is why I rejoice today.”
Ananias, Azariah, Mishael.
Are you rejoicing today
at the feast of the holy archangel Michael?
“Yes,” said the three holy saints.
“We rejoice and are glad, because the one whose feast you celebrate today is the one who came into the middle of the blazing fiery furnace.
He extinguished it for us.
He made the king believe in God.
Our martyrdom was brought to completion.
That is why we rejoice today.” Daniel, man greatly beloved,
are you too rejoicing today at this great feast?
I think you rejoice even more. Daniel said, “And what other joy is equal to my joy?
For it was not just once,
nor was it twice, that I saw Michael, the true prince.
And when they threw me into the lions’ den,
Michael, the commander-in-chief, was the one who came to me and shut the mouths of the lions.
That is why I rejoice today.”
The twelve apostles, are you rejoicing today at this great feast? “We rejoice,” they said, “because after this great sorrow that befell us
when they crucified our Lord Jesus Christ,
and while we were hiding for fear of the Jews, Mary the virgin came and told us, ‘I went with those who were with me to see the tomb early on Sunday.
We found the holy archangel Michael.
He rolled away the stone and sat down on it.
And he gave us the good news that the Lord had risen.
That is why I rejoice today.’”
Saint Zechariah the priest and John his son.
They too rejoice at the feast of the holy archangel Michael.
“Yes,” the saints said, “we rejoice,
since he appointed the archangel as his commander-in-chief.
I too am his priest. And my son John is the son of Elizabeth, who is a relative of Mary, the mother of Jesus, my relative by birth.
That is why we rejoice today.”
Stephen, the chief deacon
and first martyr, do you too rejoice today at the feast of Michael the archangel?
“Yes,” he said, “my joy is great,
because, at the time when they stoned me,
I raised my eyes and saw that the heavens had opened. I saw Michael the archangel and all his angels praying for me.
And I saw Jesus standing at the right hand of the Father.
That is why I rejoice today.”
All you martyrs and righteous people,
do you rejoice at Michael’s feast today?
“Yes,” the saints said, “we truly rejoice today,
because, in every affliction that overtook us and every torture inflicted on us,
it was Michael the archangel who gave us strength, and we endured them until we completed our struggle and received honors.
That is why we rejoice today.”
All the heavenly orders also rejoice with us today at the festival of the holy archangel Michael. “Yes,” they said, “all the joy is ours, from the time
when our Creator overthrew the proud one and established over us the humble one, the great holy archangel Michael. That is why we rejoice today.”
Truly, my beloved, great is the honor of this feast today, which is spread out for us not only on earth but also in heaven. Now then, you listeners who love learning,
Let us too make every effort to be found at Michael’s festival, so that we too may eat
of the countless good things laid up for us, together with all the saints whose names we have mentioned.
Perhaps, my beloved, we might dare to go to the commander-in-chief’s banquet without being properly dressed,
but go in filthy clothes, with our bodies also full of dirt, and you would find us in shame among those who are dressed, as they pull their robes close around themselves
and recoil from us, lest we draw near to them and they become defiled by us.

And after suspicion of this kind, they would throw us out. For these are certainly the words that those who are properly dressed will say to us: “You foolish people! Are you not ashamed to be like this?
And even if you feel no shame, do you not fear the true King, Jesus Christ,
and his holy archangel Michael? Do you not know whose courtyard this is?
and whose banquet this is?”
If not, [?] the king and his holy archangel Michael, the commander-in-chief who prevails in battles before his lord, who gives him all these honors because of his strength.
Truly, I am amazed at you: how did you dare to enter the inner courtyard?
And especially with your other body parts exposed!
Did you not hear him saying, “Do not enter
my wedding hall without wearing a wedding garment”?
Or have you not heard about him, about the man who dared—
He entered wearing a dirty garment, just like you.
You know what happened to him.
It is written that he had him bound hand and foot and threw him into the outer darkness. There will be weeping there
and gnashing of teeth.
Now then, brothers and sisters, withdraw to the outer courtyard, a little distance from the door,
so that when our Lord the King enters with his great holy archangel, you may plead with him. Perhaps he will have a little mercy on you.
in addition to the rest of those who receive charity at the entrance to the courtyard. For the archangel whose feast you are celebrating is merciful.
He will not abandon you on any account. But save yourselves.
Do not let them find you in this corrupt state in the midst
of today's feast, so that we do not share in the suffering of the others.
Look, I have told you, and you have heard, my beloved, the rebukes that these people had to bear.
And especially since those speaking to them are people like themselves,
and not God. But perhaps someone will say to me, “What are these dirty clothes, or what are these bodily adornments?
Is there favoritism with God? Or does God love the rich person more than the poor person? Do I not want to dress up too?
Does anyone want to be insulted?”
No, that is not how it is, my beloved.
May we never say that God shows favoritism and loves the rich person more than the poor person.
But listen, and I will tell you about the good garment and the dirty one. When you come to Michael's banquet, anoint your head, wash your face, and cast hypocrisy away from you.
And you will be properly fit to attend.
If you are invited to Michael's banquet, cleanse your heart of all malice and all slander, and your garment will be beautiful.
And you will be properly worthy.
If you enter the church of God, which is the house of Michael—
Keep yourself away from sexual immorality, every passion, and every defilement.
Clothe yourself in peace, purity, and righteousness.
And you will enter the court with joy and celebrate with the holy archangel Michael when you are invited to the wedding of the king and his great commander.
May your acts of mercy and love open the door of the bridal chamber for you.
And whatever you give, you will find repaid tenfold on your table before you.
If you wish to honor Michael, the king’s chief commander,
let the widows and orphans leave your presence with cheerful faces and their bodies clothed, according to your means.
And I tell you that your gift will be great in the sight of God and the archangel Michael. If you wish to go joyfully to Michael’s banquet, then welcome strangers into your home
at Michael’s feast and show them mercy.
And Michael will come out joyfully and lead you in peace into his king’s court.
If someone pleads with you, asking you for anything in Michael’s name, do not hesitate to give it to him.
I tell you, my beloved, that what you will give to the person—
Michael is the one who will take it in his hands and offer it [?] to God on your behalf.
And he will repay you for them, with their return, on earth.
And God will have mercy on you in his kingdom, for it is written, “Mercy triumphs over judgment.”
And also, “I will establish mercy for you.”
If you persist in celebrating the feast of the archangel Michael once each month, on the twelfth day,
on the day of his appointment, and you neglect to take care of his offering and provide a service according to your ability. He will remain.
the archangel Michael, in turn, will plead with God for you at all times, so that he may grant you everything you need, beyond what you imagine.
But perhaps, my beloved, you will say to me, “If I give charitable gifts and offerings, will I be giving them to God?”
“Is Michael a god, that I should offer my sacrifice to him? There is no god besides the God of heaven, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.”
For my part, I will answer you: “Well said, believer! Truly, a believer is someone whose faith is directed toward his Lord.”
But listen, everyone, and let me explain to you.
Is it not one king who rules over the territories, with many ranks of officials under him?
And among these ranks you will find one higher than another, while the king is higher than them all.
But if someone forms a friendship
with one of these ranks of royal officials and gives him honors and money,
are these given to him in the rank to which he belongs?
No, rather, they give them to him knowing that his rank is great
and that he is close to the king at all times.
And he can save him from every danger, also recommending him to the king
as a worthy man,
so that others may receive favor through him. This is also how it is with everyone who gives charitable meals and offerings to God on Michael’s day: the archangel receives their sacrifices from them,
and their charitable gifts, and he will give them to God like a great fragrant offering. He will receive an order from God concerning them, and he will prepare many good things for them.
and accepts them as gifts before God, so that they may be free from punishment forever.
But if you want to understand how, for what people give as charitable meals
and offerings to God on the day
of the holy archangel Michael, he serves them while they are in the world,
listen to this great and wonderful account, to the glory of God and his holy archangel Michael.
There was a righteous man who loved God and charitable meals, living in our region, who had a wise wife,
and a dignified one.
She too was perfect in mercy and charity, just like her husband.
They had great confidence in the protection of the archangel Michael.
The man’s name was Dorotheus, and his wife’s name was Theopiste.
From the time they were joined together, when both of them were young,
they possessed a well-appointed estate that their parents had left them.
They had many livestock and a great deal of money for the needs of this world.
Now these holy people, Dorotheus and his wife Theopiste, had a custom of honoring the holy archangel Michael: whenever the twelfth day of each month approached,
they would prepare the offering on the eleventh, for the following day, the twelfth,
early in the morning, and send the firstfruits and the offering to the archangel’s sanctuary with joy.
Afterward they would slaughter a sheep and prepare pots of its meat
and vegetables, and bake loaves of bread as needed.
When they had received the holy mysteries, they would invite every needy person they could find, along with the blind and the lame.
and the widows, the orphans, and the strangers.
and those whom they find, and they bring them into their homes, and both of them stand before them and serve them until they have finished eating.
And they give them plenty of wine.
When they see them leaving, they anoint their heads with oil and send them off joyfully, saying, “Go in peace, beloved brothers.”
For we have been found worthy of a great gift.
You have come to us today.
They did these things every twelfth day, so that their sweet fragrance and their love would rise to God in heaven,
while everyone honored them throughout their lives because of their excellence.
And they concealed their virtue; they did not seek any human glory at all.
Instead, all their hope rested in God
and the archangel Michael.
Now it happened, after a long time during which they continued in this way, that God gave an order.
The ascent took place so that the water would not come over the land, as a punishment for human beings because of their sins.
Then he held it back for three consecutive years.
So the land of Egypt fell into great turmoil,
along with those who lived on it, and they forgot the abundance in Egypt, as it is written.
Then many people and animals died,
Because no rain had come upon the earth for three consecutive years, the holy man, however,
He and his wife did not stop what they did every month, pleading with God and the holy archangel Michael:
